sources.note: Nothing. en: 'a meeting between a Kanamarí and the Flecheiros was observed, showing that the two have different languages. Their language is thus unknown and unattested.' Also: 'Similarities in arrow design with another "uncontacted" tribe contacted by the Kanamari, the Tsohom Djapa "toucan people", who speak the same language as the Kanamarí, suggest that the Flecheiros may be related to or the same as them.' pt: 'foi observado um encontro entre Kanamarí e Flecheiro, mostrando que os dois possuem idiomas diferentes, ainda desconhecida.'

sources.note: Nothing. The FUNAI register list (pp. 24-25) has '34 • Igarapé Flecheira' among three 'registros em estudo' in TI Vale do Javari (no ethnographic or linguistic detail). The Vale do Javari chapter by Beto Marubo (pp. 124-125) says most Javari languages are Pano (Marubo, Mayoruna, Matis, Korubo, Kulina) and 'apenas os Kanamari e Tyohom-Dyapa falam línguas de outra família linguística (Katukina)'; it does not name the Flecheiros or say what they speak. A FUNAI staff interview (p. ~?) mentions localization expeditions to unconfirmed references 'no Arrojo, Batã, Jaquirana, Flecheira'.

sources.note: Nothing. The page has no descriptive references at all (only three 'wordlist_or_less' overview items: Ricardo 1986, Walker et al. 2016, Ricardo & Gongora 2019). Comment: 'The Flecheiros is one of the uncontacted peoples in the Javari region (Ricardo 1986). If anything, Ethnographic considerations would point to the language being Kanamarí [knm]. But since Wallace 2011 recounts one meeting between a Kanamarí and the Flecheiros, showing that the two have different languages, they arguably speak a language not counted already in E16...E28.'
